title: Defect Interactions ε-martensite, Stacking Fault, and Twin Interfaces in Hydrogen Precharged Austenitic Stainless Steel
content: Austenitic stainless steels (SS) are widely used in nuclear applications and in operational environments for which hydrogen exposure can affect the mechanical properties [1, 2]. Previous deformation studies of 304L SS have shown that the presence of hydrogen can promote ε-martensite formation within deformation bands [3]. Within these deformation bands there is a mixture of twins and ε-martensite lathes with stacking faults. An example of such a deformation band is shown in Figure 1(a). The interaction and intersection of deformation bands with twins, stacking faults, ε-lathes are of particular interest to understand deformation of SS.
